name: ASCII / terminal CRT
look: all characters, monospace grid, phosphor glow, typed output.

fits.notes: dev tools, CLIs, agents, security, hacker culture

when_not: Avoid for consumer lifestyle or anything non-technical.

type.guidance: JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Berkeley Mono
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Berkeley Mono; green/amber/white on black.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: phosphor colour is the brand colour; falls back to green or amber if it is too dark
brand_lock.type_role: a monospace; brand face for the claim line
brand_lock.world_changes: all characters on a monospace grid, typed output, scanlines
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: video-to-ASCII conversion (sample brightness to glyph ramp)
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: portrait or product photo of {subject}, high contrast, plain background, to be converted to ASCII

animate_with.what: displacement / warp (shader fed by noise or depth)

codex_assets.r1_note: an image to convert to ASCII (portrait, product); A3.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

build.engine_meaning: buildable today / reference only (builder hand-codes it)
build.recipe: `styles/ascii-crt.md`, `personalities/retro-terminal.json`, `systems/vernacular/terminal-crt.md`. Canvas glyph grid, shader scanlines; ASCII-ify a render target by sampling to a glyph atlas. close-c9 typed-prompt exists.

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: Green phosphor
palettes.words: black-green screen, bright phosphor green, near-white

palettes.name: Paper terminal
palettes.words: warm paper, black text, rust, blue

brand_lock.rule: Phosphor colour is the brand colour if bright enough on black; else green or amber. Prompt and cursor take the brand colour; background stays near-black. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: All type is monospace on a fixed grid (1 glyph = 0.6em wide); the real claim sets in the brand face.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: monospace grid 120x34 chars; prompt line at the bottom; all elements are characters
composition.fill: text fills 60-80%; images become glyph ramps
composition.product_ui: UI shown as a screen-in-terminal capture inside a CRT window; or the UI's data is rendered as ASCII first and resolves to the real UI

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: flat monitor-on-desk shot, 35 mm, slight CRT curvature, shallow depth of field. Lighting: self-lit phosphor, soft bloom spilling onto the dark room. Material: glass CRT with phosphor glow, scanlines, subtle dust on the screen. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: scanlines, glow bloom, tiny horizontal flicker. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no modern flat UI, no anti-aliased sans, no colour photos, no extra colours beyond the phosphor ramp, no readable invented text.
codex.camera: flat monitor-on-desk shot, 35 mm, slight CRT curvature, shallow depth of field
codex.lighting: self-lit phosphor, soft bloom spilling onto the dark room
codex.material: glass CRT with phosphor glow, scanlines, subtle dust on the screen
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: scanlines, glow bloom, tiny horizontal flicker
negatives: no extra colours beyond the phosphor ramp

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: glass CRT with phosphor glow; flat monitor-on-desk shot; black-green screen, bright phosphor green, near-white.

sprite_sheet.rules: Not a sprite style. For a cut-out object or character use --transparent (flat #00FF00 key, then despill); one subject, no shadow plane.

do: Everything on the character grid, always
Type with a typewriter reveal at irregular human speed
Convert one image to ASCII as the signature beat
dont: No proportional fonts in the world
No smooth fades: cut or type
cheap_ways: Matrix green rain with no relevance
Faux-terminal text with no real commands
Overbloomed glow that blurs the glyphs
